1lnspuy: The youth association is preparing an exhibition of neighborhood photographs. The opening date has been announced for the twentieth, but two decisions are still missing. The cultural center must confirm the room, and the people in the portraits have to authorize the use of their images. The team wants to move forward without treating as settled what depends on others.
nf00r4: Once they receive confirmation of the room, they will measure the walls and decide how many photographs they can hang. Meanwhile, they can select images and write the texts. They won't print the portraits until they have the corresponding permissions. Before the material arrives, two volunteers will check the lighting and the route through the room. As soon as that check is finished, they will send a list of needs to the coordinator. Each step has a person responsible, so that everyone doesn't assume someone else is taking care of it.
18g7dyy: They will send the task list to each person in charge. The coordinator wants to go over it with the team before circulating it, to make sure nobody gets an old version of the calendar.
1w4i5pd: The plan includes a three-day margin for solving difficulties. If the room isn't available, they will use a smaller selection in the library lobby. It isn't their preferred option, but it lets them keep the event with the neighbors. The coordinator points out that a calendar doesn't eliminate unexpected problems: it helps you recognize what changes when one appears. The goal is not to carry out every detail of the first sketch, but to open an exhibition that is understandable, respectful, and possible with the resources they actually have.
